inputs.original_text: Folks, once again we see the fundamental breakdown of order when unions and public sector bodies think they can just hold the nation hostage. The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has just slapped a one-month ultimatum on the federal government, demanding the conclusion of the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions. They are threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if their demands are unmet, showing a complete disregard for national stability and the education of our youth. This kind of militancy—stemming right out of the union’s 54th National Executive Council resolutions—undermines authority, disrupts the natural order of our institutions, and proves that accountability and personal responsibility have taken a backseat to relentless agitation. Instead of respecting proper governance and working towards cultural continuity, these groups choose disruption, threatening to bring everything to a grinding halt just to get their way.
inputs.modified_text:
Folks, look at this. Once again, we see the absolute collapse of basic discipline and respect for authority. The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has just slapped a one-month ultimatum on the federal government, demanding the conclusion of the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions. They are threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if their demands are unmet, showing a complete disregard for national stability and the education of our youth. 

This is what happens when militant groups think they can hold the nation hostage. Stemming right out of the union’s 54th National Executive Council resolutions, this kind of behavior completely undermines rightful authority, shatters the natural order of our institutions, and proves that personal responsibility and accountability have been thrown out the window in favor of relentless, selfish agitation. Instead of respecting proper governance, traditional structures, and working towards the stability of our society, these agitators choose chaos and disruption. They are ready to bring everything to a grinding halt just to get their way, trampling on the future of our youth and spitting on the very idea of national duty. We cannot let this kind of lawlessness dictate the terms of our society.
